title: Flame Towers
visualBrief: Three independent curved triangular glazed flames, with unequal heights, pointed swept crowns, unitized facade panels, dark maintenance slots, pale stepped retail pavilions and a glazed central atrium.

sourceFacts.heightPrecision: Rounded whole meters published by the Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat; independent engineer above-ground approximations differ with local entry datum.
sourceFacts.facadeSystem: Four-corner story-height unitized glazing, curved surfaces optimized from the original NURBS geometry
sourceFacts.primaryIdentityOverride: HOK identifies south residential, north hotel and west office; inconsistent OSM hotel/commercial tags are retained in evidence, not used to swap these roles.
sourceFacts.facadePose: Daytime; behind-glass LED media is inactive

reconstruction.plan: Each curved triangular tower has its own attributed mapped ring and outward crown axis. Three unequal heights and native cardinal frame retain the ensemble arrangement, without replacing the complex with a single bounding-box tower.
reconstruction.facade: Continuous quadrilateral blue-grey glazing follows the curved shell; source floor and plan sampling provides subtle panel tint variation. Paired upper and partial lower dark maintenance slots are retained. Three-centimetre individual mullions are below the medium-fi extent threshold and omitted, rather than modeled as repeated closed cell frames. Shared stone and coated-metal textures supply podium and trim; no visible diagonal grid or animated LED texture is baked into the shaft.
reconstruction.crown: Curved pointed flicks follow a smooth vertical contraction of the mapped wing plan, with an outward apex. Their exact NURBS definition is not published in the available primary references, so sectional curvature and pane pitch remain explicit reconstructions.
reconstruction.podium: The mapped common retail base has individually glazed fronts; eastern stepped stone pavilions, central barrel-glazed atrium, small curved terrace pool, west-central red cinema and north hotel canopy follow the engineer aerial photograph. Fine dimensions and elevations are photograph-derived.

geometrySource: Original deterministic exterior geometry; no downloaded meshes or copied photographic textures. Footprint-derived registration includes separately attributed OpenStreetMap evidence.
sourceLicense: Original reconstruction under repository license. Map-derived plan evidence: © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0. Reference publications are linked, not redistributed.
materialMethod: Canonical shared material graphs bound through molenSurface extras with metric coordinates divided by central repeat meters. Vertex colors provide component tint. Glass retains opaque metallic-roughness PBR; no bitmap texture copies per model.
reviewStatus: source-geometry; near/far and shared-material captures pending
limitations: Original68737triangles/7786092byte detailed master remains exactly reproducible through unchanged buildFlame recipe. Reviewed source retains original1.36m Hermite-sampled plan and original floor datums, curved pointed crowns, paired/partial dark maintenance slots, cut common podium, three stepped picture-window pavilions, curved roof pool, red cinema, glazed barrel atrium, hotel canopy and two cylindrical doors. Continuous atrium shell and merged frame strips reduce repeated pane islands; retained canopy/roof geometry closes the exterior. Skyline uses coarse wing sections and averaged shared graph colours with a continuous podium and closed stone pavilions, omitting fine maintenance slots, pavilion windows/skylights, vents and door framing. District restores dark maintenance bands, cut podium and pavilion windows; street restores facade sampling and sparse vent/joint sampling; close-up restores original facade/ring detail and entry hardware. Canonical limestone approximates concrete; coated-metal and one opaque palette-glass group retain three near draw groups with zero embedded images. Exact NURBS control points, hillside grading, section pitch, slot elevations and pavilion/entrance dimensions remain reconstructions; no surveyed terrain or physical-device-performance claim. Finite twelve-ray comparisons at six heights per tower use4/1.5/.5/.1m skyline/district/street/close-up along-ray allowances, excluding omitted fine trim; the804triangle ensemble skyline is deliberately coarser than the separately authored single-tower skylines. This is not a global Hausdorff bound.
importReason: Preserve thin facade frames, panel joints and crown/antenna details until a measured LOD chain is authored.
